messages:
anya (product): Quick sync — customers keep pushing for streaming that supports resume + structured output. Need a concrete set of launch gates (latency SLO, resume window, finish_reason taxonomy, SDK helpers). Who can own the spec?

mike (eng-runtime): +1. Main infra tradeoffs: SSE is simpler for HTTP stacks and plays nicer with our existing load balancers; Websockets give lower tail-latency and bi-directional flow. Resumability requires server-side session state (KV for KV-cache offsets).

omar (eng-ml): For structured outputs and function/tool calling, streaming deltas will often be partial JSON fragments. We must define canonical delta shapes and a clear finish_reason set: "stop", "error", "function_call_complete", "truncated". Also define how partial function arguments are reassembled.

lina (devex): Docs perspective: mobile and flaky networks are big asks. Recommend returning an opaque "resume_token" in the final event and supporting a resume endpoint `/v1/streams/resume?token=...`. Will sketch examples for both SSE and WS. :memo:

sam (support): Customers will expect SDK methods to rehydrate state and resume from token. If we only publish raw protocol docs, support tickets will spike. SDK plan is a product requirement imo.

mike (eng-runtime): Implementation note: consider shipping SSE-first in hosted API (v1.1) because it avoids sticky sessions and proxies; add optional WS in Dedicated/private. SSE semantics we can rely on: `event:` types, `data:` frames, and `retry:` hints. Resume window: suggest 30s for live low-latency, but allow configurable TTL for Dedicated.

anya (product): Launch gates proposal: 1) explicit resume contract + example code; 2) delta format for structured outputs (line-delimited JSON or "chunked-json"); 3) finish_reason mapping & docs; 4) reference SDK helpers for JS + mobile; 5) 1 customer pilot and perf SLOs (p50/p95 token latency). Agree?

omar (eng-ml): Add a quality gate: function_call must always emit a final event with finish_reason:function_call_complete and the full reconstructed payload. If we fail to do that, downstream systems will be inconsistent.

lina (devex): Drafting now. Example SSE stream (rough):
```
event: delta
data: {"delta":{"content":"Hel"},"tok_idx":123}

event: delta
data: {"delta":{"content":"lo"},"tok_idx":124}

event: finish
data: {"finish_reason":"stop","resume_token":"abc123"}
```

mike (eng-runtime): A few edge cases to call out in the spec: 1) proxy buffering can coalesce SSE chunks — clients should parse by event boundaries not by line count. 2) Backpressure: enforce tokens/sec per connection and include explicit `retry` or `rate_hint` event. 3) Resume tokens must be short-lived and single-use if they tie to KV offsets.

anya (product): Good callouts. Also we need to decide on the delta encoding for structured outputs: do we use full JSON patch objects, or simple partial text deltas with token indices? Tradeoffs: JSON patch is explicit but heavier; token deltas are smaller but require precise reassembly. Input?

omar (eng-ml): Prefer token-indexed deltas for efficiency, but we must provide a robust reassembly reference impl in SDK to avoid inconsistency across languages.

lina (devex): I'll produce two examples and a migration note (how to fall back to non-streaming completions).

sam (support): I'll draft FAQ bits for common resume failures and how to triage.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for streams-api v1.1

anya (product): Thanks everyone — can we have a short spec + checklist by EOW and a proposed customer pilot list? :calendar:
